problem.label: The Gap
problem.headline: Many Data Sources. No Architecture to Connect Them.
problem.p1: Most clubs sit on more performance data than ever before. The problem is not volume. It is that the data lives in disconnected systems with no individual model underneath it. No standardised infrastructure. No consolidation strategy. No security architecture built for clinical data. Twinspire is the structured layer that connects what is already being collected.
problem.p2: The data your players generate off the training pitch — rest-day recovery scores, sleep quality, nocturnal HRV — often sits outside the club's performance environment. Combining these signals with training load can give staff a richer longitudinal view of how an individual is responding.
problem.p3: Combining recovery monitoring with training load provides a richer basis for modelling the athlete as a dynamic system. Twinspire's research programme is testing which combinations of signals add meaningful explanatory value at the individual level, and under what conditions.
problem.originHeading: The Data Existed. The Context Didn't.
problem.originBody: Twinspire began as control engineering research at DTU, applying digital twin methodology to physiological systems. The same principles used to model complex industrial systems — building an individual dynamic model, learning baseline behaviour, and detecting meaningful deviation — were applied to the athlete. The research became a product when Pouya recognised that the gap between what the data showed and what the clinical team knew was not a communication problem. It was an infrastructure problem. Twinspire has been developed from the outset with EU MDR requirements informing the development, governance and validation approach, with security and data provenance treated as foundations rather than feature layers.

product.p1: When your doctor runs blood tests, they track your values over time because your normal may differ from the reference range. Twinspire applies the same longitudinal principle across athlete performance and recovery data, building an individual reference rather than relying on a squad average alone.

card1.title: Not a squad benchmark
card1.body: A shift that looks unremarkable across a squad can be meaningful for a particular player. Each individual's reference behaviour is built and measured separately.

card2.title: Trained staff leave. The model does not.
card2.body: Experienced staff build valuable contextual knowledge about long-term players. Twinspire is designed to preserve longitudinal physiological context when staff, systems or clubs change.

card3.title: The Athletic Passport
card3.body: The portable, athlete-centred representation of the Individual Physiological Response Profile: what the model has learned about how that athlete responds over time. With appropriate permissions and governance, that context can move with the athlete when they transfer.

product.p2: Players connect supported personal wearables and complete a morning check-in directly in the Twinspire app. This is one way the personal data stream can enter the model. The daily check-in captures subjective readiness, sleep quality and wellness markers alongside wearable-derived signals. If your club already has a player-facing app, Twinspire can integrate with it rather than sit alongside it.

faq.title: Frequently Asked
faq.subtitle: The questions clubs, athletes, and partners ask most often.

whatIsTwinspire.question: What is Twinspire?
whatIsTwinspire.answer: Twinspire connects club and athlete data and builds a continuously updated individual physiological model for each athlete. It learns what is normal for that individual and surfaces meaningful deviations, contributing signals and longitudinal context for performance and medical staff. It is a decision support tool, not a replacement for clinical judgment.

whatProblemDoesTwinspireSolve.question: What problem does Twinspire solve?
whatProblemDoesTwinspireSolve.answer: Clubs collect valuable data across GPS, strength, clinical systems and other tools, while athletes may generate recovery, sleep and HRV data away from the club. These streams are rarely interpreted together through a continuously updated individual model. Twinspire connects relevant data under a structured governance framework, learns each athlete's baseline and surfaces meaningful deviations with the contributing signals for staff to interpret.

whoIsTwinspireFor.question: Who is Twinspire for?
whoIsTwinspireFor.answer: Twinspire is built for physiotherapists, medical teams, coaches, performance staff and athletes who need a coherent longitudinal understanding of individual response rather than isolated data points or population averages alone.

howDoesTwinspireWork.question: How does it actually work?
howDoesTwinspireWork.answer: Relevant club and athlete data feed an individual baseline model. Twinspire learns what normal looks like for each athlete, monitors how that state changes over time, and surfaces meaningful deviation together with the signals driving it. Outputs can feed back into the club's existing workflow.

whatIsAthleticPassport.question: What is the Athletic Passport?
whatIsAthleticPassport.answer: The Athletic Passport is the portable, athlete-centred representation of an athlete's Individual Physiological Response Profile: the longitudinal understanding Twinspire develops of how that athlete responds to training, recovery and physical stress. With appropriate permissions and governance, relevant profile information can move with the athlete between clubs without implying that every underlying source dataset transfers.

isTwinspireDashboard.question: Is this just another dashboard?
isTwinspireDashboard.answer: No. A dashboard displays variables. Twinspire is designed as a decision support system: it builds an individual baseline model, monitors change across relevant data streams, and surfaces meaningful deviation with the specific drivers behind it. The output is decision support with visible reasoning — the relevant deviation, contributing signals and longitudinal context rather than an isolated score.

whatIsDigitalTwin.question: What does individual baseline modeling mean in practice?
whatIsDigitalTwin.answer: Twinspire builds a continuously evolving model of what is normal for a specific athlete across time. Rather than treating a population reference or squad average as the whole answer, it compares current signals with that athlete's own longitudinal baseline and response history.

whatDataDoesTwinspireUse.question: What data does Twinspire use?
whatDataDoesTwinspireUse.answer: Depending on the club setup and permissions, Twinspire can integrate training and movement data, strength and testing outputs, clinical context, subjective check-ins and supported wearable-derived recovery, sleep and physiological signals. Data access and processing depend on the relevant governance, agreements and permissions for each source.

whoOwnsData.question: Who owns the player data?
whoOwnsData.answer: Different data has different governance. Club-generated source data, athlete-provided data and Twinspire-derived longitudinal information may be handled under different roles and agreements. The Athletic Passport is designed to be athlete-centred and portable, while source data remains subject to the applicable permissions, contracts and data-protection framework. Twinspire processes data under formal Data Processing Agreements and does not sell personal data.

isTwinspireGdprCompliant.question: How does Twinspire approach GDPR?
isTwinspireGdprCompliant.answer: Twinspire has been designed around GDPR-aligned data practices, EU-based hosting and processing, formal Data Processing Agreements and role-based access controls. Consent is used where applicable, alongside the wider governance and lawful-basis framework required for each processing context.

whereIsTwinspireBased.question: Where is Twinspire based and who built it?
whereIsTwinspireBased.answer: Twinspire was developed from research at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) in Copenhagen. It was started by Pouya Tobias Strand Nikoui, a former professional footballer who returned to DTU after experiencing the gap between fragmented monitoring data and individual context. The team combines expertise in AI, individual athlete modelling, platform architecture, research and data security.

dataEthics.heading: The Compliance Architecture
dataEthics.subtitle: Most sports platforms were built for performance, then had compliance retrofitted. Twinspire started from the other direction.
dataEthics.description: As player unions and club legal teams scrutinise how health and performance data is handled, the compliance architecture your platform is built on matters.
dataEthics.card1: Model inputs are selected for physiological relevance and traceability. The validation programme is testing which variables and combinations provide meaningful explanatory value for individual athlete state and response.
dataEthics.card2: Validation is treated as part of the development lifecycle, not a post-launch add-on. Twinspire has been developed from the outset with EU MDR requirements informing its development, governance and validation approach.
dataEthics.card3: Granular and transparent. Athletes can understand and manage relevant sharing permissions and consent where applicable; access is role-based and context-specific.
dataEthics.card4: Standardised ingestion across club and personal streams. Data sources enter through controlled pipelines designed for consistency, auditability and traceability.
dataEthics.disclaimer: Twinspire is a decision support platform. It is not intended to diagnose or treat medical conditions.
dataEthics.card5: Interpretable by design. Outputs surface the signals behind meaningful deviation so staff can see what is changing and interpret it in context.

digitalTwin.sectionLabel: What a Decision Support System Actually Is
digitalTwin.heading: A dashboard displays variables
digitalTwin.headingAccent: It does not explain what matters, why it matters, or what to do next
digitalTwin.intro: At ECSS 2026, independent researchers proposed a checklist for what a genuine individual athlete model requires. Below is where Twinspire stands, honestly.

individualized.label: Individualized
individualized.body: Every metric measured against that player's own evolving baseline, not a squad average, not a population norm.

dynamicallyUpdated.label: Dynamically Updated
dynamicallyUpdated.body: The model updates continuously with new relevant data. The aim is to improve the longitudinal understanding of each athlete over time.

connectedToDecisions.label: Connected to Decisions
connectedToDecisions.body: Output is framed as decision support: current state, meaningful deviation, contributing signals and longitudinal context presented inside the workflow where staff make decisions.

explicitAboutUncertainty.label: Explicit About Uncertainty
explicitAboutUncertainty.body: Key drivers are surfaced explicitly. Staff see which signals are driving a deviation rather than receiving a single unexplained score.

validatedAgainstOutcomes.label: Validated Against Outcomes
validatedAgainstOutcomes.body: The current validation programme is designed to test how model outputs relate to meaningful real-world outcomes.

digitalTwin.closingNote: This checklist did not originate with us. We think it is a useful standard to be measured against.

passport.heading: Your club can change,
passport.headingAccent: your physiological context does not have to reset
passport.intro: When an athlete changes clubs, much of the contextual understanding built over time can be lost or fragmented across systems. Twinspire is designed to preserve the individual physiological context that can appropriately travel with the athlete.
passport.howItWorks: The Athletic Passport is the portable, athlete-centred representation of the Individual Physiological Response Profile: what the model has learned about how that athlete responds to training, recovery and physical stress over time. With appropriate permissions and governance, that context can move with the athlete when they transfer.
passport.forClubs: For clubs: relevant longitudinal context on a new signing from day one, where permissions allow. For players: a career-long physiological response profile designed to remain portable across systems and clubs.
passport.differentiator: The commercial opportunity is longitudinal continuity: preserving an athlete's individual physiological context across changes in club, staff and technology rather than rebuilding that understanding from zero each time.

intro.p1: At Twinspire, we're developing a digital twin platform for individualised athlete modelling in elite football. Our work sits at the intersection of sports science, data, and performance environments where outcomes matter. Decisions are made under uncertainty, often with incomplete information. That's the context we build for.
intro.p2: We are a small team with a broad range of experience, from early 20s to mid-60s. What unites us is a shared approach: we take ownership, we focus on execution, and we prefer clarity over complexity. There is little interest here in unnecessary process or work that doesn't translate into something tangible.
intro.p3: There is often a perceived trade-off between experience and willingness to build. We do not think that holds. Some people naturally stay close to the work, regardless of seniority. Those are the people we value: individuals who take responsibility, contribute directly, and care about what they produce.
intro.p4: We work out of DTU in Copenhagen, with the flexibility to work from home. We operate with a high level of trust and expect people to manage their time accordingly. We are an international and diverse team, and we see that as a strength.
intro.p5: What you can expect is meaningful ownership, a direct connection between your work and its impact, and an environment where things move without unnecessary friction. We are early, and we are ambitious, which practically means that you'll have the opportunity to shape both the product and how it is being built.
intro.p6: If this sounds like the kind of place you want to contribute, we'd like to hear from you. If you don't see an opening that fits you, reach out regardless. We are growing.
